note: Demonstration archive only. A demo is not a commercial product. Walking, waving or sitting in a car does not establish autonomy. Remote assistance is unknown unless a named source disclosed it. Specs Tesla stated on stage stay labelled as company claims. We Robot 2024 and other events stay off this list until a source is opened.

demos.title: AI Day 2021 — Tesla Bot announced
demos.lede: Tesla announced a humanoid robot and showed drawings plus a non-working stage figure. The opened source does not describe a walking machine.
shown: Drawings of a planned Tesla Bot near the end of AI Day.
A mannequin version on the stage that was not working, as reported by The Verge.
notShown: Walking, object handling, or factory work.

autonomy.note: No robot task was shown. Autonomy is not established.

remoteAssistance.note: Not disclosed in the opened source.

uncertain: Whether the stage figure was a mannequin, as The Verge wrote in 2021, or a person in a suit, as Musk later said at AI Day 2022.
Whether any of the stated size, weight or face-screen figures were more than a concept slide.
companyClaims: About 5 ft 8 in, 125 lb, screen for a face — Tesla figures reported by The Verge, not independently measured here.
A prototype 'sometime next year' (The Verge's wording of Musk).

source.title: Elon Musk says Tesla is working on humanoid robots

laterNote.text: At AI Day 2022 Musk said they had 'a guy in a suit' the year before.

demos.title: AI Day 2022 — walking prototype on stage
demos.generation: Optimus prototype (Bumble C plus a stand unit)
demos.lede: Tesla showed a walking prototype and a separate body on a stand. The Verge recorded what happened live versus what was only on video or claimed.
shown: A unit Tesla called Bumble C walked forward and did a 'raise the roof' move.
Video clips of a robot picking up boxes — shown as recordings, not as the live stage act.
A 'very close to production' body held up on a stand; it waved, showing wrist and hand range. Workers later rolled that unit off.
notShown: The production-looking unit walking under its own power.

autonomy.note: The Verge reported Tesla moved Autopilot software onto the bot and used motion capture plus inverse kinematics. Completing a staged walk or a recorded box pickup does not establish autonomy.

remoteAssistance.note: The opened source does not say whether anyone was driving the robot remotely.

uncertain: How much of the live walk was scripted, limited, or assisted.
Whether the recorded box-pickup clips were the same unit, the same software, or the same constraints as the stage walk.
companyClaims: Musk said this was 'the first time it operated without a tether' — on stage that night (company claim via The Verge).
2.3 kWh pack, Tesla SoC, Wi-Fi and LTE, six actuator types, biologically inspired hands — Tesla engineering claims reported by The Verge, not measured here.

source.title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveils prototype humanoid Optimus robot

demos.title: Roadster reveal — Optimus in the driver's seat
demos.generation: Optimus (generation not stated by the opened source)
demos.lede: When the Roadster door opened after programmed stunts, an Optimus robot was in the seat. Engadget says that was for show. The opened source is about the car, not a robot demo.
shown: An Optimus robot seated in the Roadster when the door opened.
The car completing ramp and thruster stunts that Engadget says were programmed into the vehicle.
notShown: Optimus driving, steering, or controlling the car.

autonomy.note: Engadget reports the stunts were programmed into the car and no human was driving. That is a statement about the Roadster, not about Optimus autonomy.

remoteAssistance.note: Not disclosed for the robot. The car's path was described as programmed.

uncertain: Which Optimus generation sat in the seat.
Whether the robot was powered, posed, or doing anything beyond occupying the seat.
